description: We are team OrbitExplorer, proudly competing in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge under the specific, inspiring category "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars." Our primary mission is to build an impactful educational archive that bridges the gap between historical space data and the next generation of young space enthusiasts.
summary: Orbit Explorer is an illustrated, story-driven educational video designed for school-age students (ages 8–14) and casual space enthusiasts. Addressing the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, our project brings NASA's silent, discarded hardware on the Moon and Mars back to life through accessible, hand-drawn style storytelling. Viewers journey through iconic missions—including Apollo Lunar Modules, Lunar Roving Vehicles, and Mars rovers like Spirit and Opportunity—to discover what these machines are, why they were sent, and the groundbreaking science they left behind. By turning complex space history into an engaging visual narrative, Orbit Explorer inspires young learners to appreciate humanity's robotic pioneers and understand how past missions pave the way for future space exploration.
details:
. What It Does & How It Works:
Orbit Explorer is an illustrated, story-driven educational video designed for school-age learners (ages 8–14) and casual space enthusiasts. Addressing the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, it guides viewers through the real stories of NASA's discarded spacecraft resting on the Moon and Mars—including Apollo Lunar Modules, Lunar Roving Vehicles, scientific surface stations, and Mars rovers like Spirit and Opportunity.
2. Benefits:
It makes complex space engineering and planetary science fun, approachable, and easy to understand for young students without overwhelming them with technical jargon. Teachers, parents, and curious kids can watch it anywhere as a ready-to-use educational story.
3. Intended Impact:
Our goal is to spark lasting curiosity about STEM and space exploration among young learners, helping them appreciate the legacy of humanity's robotic pioneers and understand how past Moon and Mars missions paved the way for future explorers.
4. Tools, Software & Super Intelligence (SI) Attribution:
Our story is grounded in official NASA Apollo and Mars Exploration mission history. We used Google NotebookLM to help structure the educational narrative, generate hand-drawn style visual illustrations (with visible watermarks retained), and produce the audio narration for our 7-minute video. We also used Gamma.app and Google Slides to build our 7-slide Project Demonstration deck, and Google Drive for public cloud hosting.
5. How Our Project Is Creative:
Instead of presenting a dry timeline or textbook summary, Orbit Explorer uses warm, hand-drawn storybook illustrations paired with first-person narrative storytelling to give NASA's silent, discarded machines a voice and personality.
6. Factors Considered:
When developing Orbit Explorer, we carefully considered three main factors: age-appropriate storytelling (keeping vocabulary clear and engaging for ages 8–14), visual pacing (using rich, illustrated scenes to keep viewers captivated throughout the 7-minute story), and scientific accuracy (verifying all mission facts and discoveries against official NASA records).
